BURSEVI:v10p313/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p313/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p313/r7.claim: God measured the kinds, individuals, qualities, acts, lifespans, forms, fortune, guidance, food, and every other feature of creation.
BURSEVI:v10p313/r7.anchor: قدر أجناس الأشياء وأنواعها وأفرادها ومقاديرها وصفاتها وأفعالها وآجالها

BURSEVI:v10p313/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p313/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v10p313/r8.claim: A Prophetic report says God measured creation fifty thousand years before creating the heavens and earth.
BURSEVI:v10p313/r8.anchor: كما قال عليه اسلام ، إن الله قدر مقادير الخلق قبل أن يخلق السموات والأرض

BURSEVI:v10p313/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p313/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p313/r9.claim: God guides each creature toward its natural or chosen function by creating inclinations, inspiration, signs, and revealed verses.
BURSEVI:v10p313/r9.anchor: فوجه كل واحد منها إلى ما يصدر عنه وينبغي له طبعا أو اختيارا ويسره لما خلق له

BURSEVI:v10p314/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p314/r1.claim: Creation's guidance appears in instinctive animal behavior, including a weasel catching a mouse and elaborate nest-building by spiders and bees.
BURSEVI:v10p314/r1.anchor: والعنكبوت تبنى بيتها على وجه عجيب غير مقدور والبشر لا يقدر على بناء البيت المسدس

BURSEVI:v10p314/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p314/r2.claim: Ants store food and split damp seeds so they will not sprout, then bring them into the sun to dry.
BURSEVI:v10p314/r2.anchor: والنمل تسعى لأعداد الذخيرة لنفسها فإذا أحست بنداوة المكان تشق الحبة نصفين

BURSEVI:v10p314/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p314/r3.claim: An observer recounts a diving bird repeatedly losing its fish to a crow, then dragging the crow underwater and escaping.
BURSEVI:v10p314/r3.anchor: قال بعضهم رأيت غواصا وهو طائر غاص وطلع بسمكة

BURSEVI:v10p314/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v10p314/r4.claim: A report warns against watering down milk for sale: a monkey exposed a dishonest seller by throwing the water's price into the sea.
BURSEVI:v10p314/r4.anchor: وفي الحديث لا تشوبوا اللبن بالماء

BURSEVI:v10p314/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p314/r5.claim: A story says a victim's dog repeatedly uncovered the well where its murdered owner lay, leading to the killer's confession and execution.
BURSEVI:v10p314/r5.anchor: وفي عجائب المخلقوت إن شخصا قتل شخصا بأصفهان وألقاه في بئر

BURSEVI:v10p314/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p314/r6.claim: Palm trees can become enamored of another tree, weakening and bearing less; binding a branch from the beloved tree to it cures the condition.
BURSEVI:v10p314/r6.anchor: ومن عجيب شجرة النخل أن يعرض لها العشق وهي أن تميل إلى نخلة أخرى

QASHANI:87:1-4/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:87:1-4/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:87:1-4/r3.claim: God deposited complete human-kind perfection in the person and guided it to be brought forth and actualized through purification and refinement.
QASHANI:87:1-4/r3.anchor: إلى إبرازه وإظهاره وإخراجه إلى الفعل بالتزكية والتصفية

SULAMI:v2p389#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p389#3/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p389#3/r1.claim: God determined felicity and misery, then made each group follow what had been allotted to it.
SULAMI:v2p389#3/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : قدر السعادة والشقاوة عليهم ثم يسر لكل واحد

SULAMI:v2p389#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p389#3/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p389#3/r2.claim: God apportioned provisions and guided people to seek them.
SULAMI:v2p389#3/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم : قدر الأرزاق وهداهم لطلبها

SULAMI:v2p389#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p389#3/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p389#3/r3.claim: God apportioned provisions and guided some to rely quietly on His guarantee instead of striving to obtain them.
SULAMI:v2p389#3/r3.anchor: قدر الأرزاق فهدى قوما بالسكون إلى ضمانه عن الحركة في طلبها

SULAMI:v2p389#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p389#3/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p389#3/r4.claim: God allotted sins and then guided their perpetrators to repentance.
SULAMI:v2p389#3/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم : قدر الذنوب عليهم بمن هداهم إلى التوبة

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416/r1.claim: Mujahid says God guided humans toward wretchedness or happiness and guided livestock to their pastures.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : والذي قدر فهدى قال : هدى الانسان للشقوة والسعادة ، وهدى الانعام لمراتعها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r1.claim: Proportioning accompanies creation and is linked by ف as its resulting effect.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r1.anchor: ولكونه مقارنا للخلقة عطف على فعل { خلق } بالفاء المفيدة للتسبب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r2.claim: Qaddara means assigning measure and bringing it into being in things and their powers; both the doubled and light readings have this meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r2.anchor: والتقدير : وضع المقدار وإيجاده في الأشياء في ذواتها وقواها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r3.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r3.claim: Most readers pronounce qaddara with a doubled dāl; al-Kisāʾī alone uses the lighter form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بالتشديد وقرأها الكسائي وحده بالتخفيف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r4.claim: Measure first means quantity by length, capacity, weight, or count; here it means creatures receive ordered configurations, organs, mental powers, and practical abilities.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r4.anchor: وأطلق هنا على تكوين المخلوقات على كيفيات منظمة مطردة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r5.claim: Repeating the relative pronoun before measuring and producing pasture highlights each attribute; فهدى then marks guidance as the effect of measure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r5.anchor: وإعادة اسم الموصول في قوله : { والذي قدر } وقوله : { والذي أخرج المرعى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r6.claim: God guides each measured thing to its assigned function: human intellect enables speech and craft, cattle are inspired to graze and nurse, and bees to gather and build honeycombs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p276/r6.anchor: فهدى كل مقدر إلى ما قدر له

TUSTARI:87:3/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:87:3/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:87:3/r1.claim: God decreed people’s felicity or wretchedness, then took charge of the felicitous and left the wretched to themselves.
TUSTARI:87:3/r1.anchor: قدر عليهم الشقاوة والسعادة، ثم تولى أهل السعادة، ووكل أهل الشقاوة إلى أنفسهم،

TUSTARI:87:3/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:87:3/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:87:3/r2.claim: Guidance has two forms: explanation and God's taking charge; an infant is inspired to its means of sustenance and mother's breast through that care.
TUSTARI:87:3/r2.anchor: والهدى هدايان: أحدهما البيان، والآخر التولي من الله تعالى، ألا ترون كيف يهتدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r1.speaker: الكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r1.claim: Al-Kisāʾī alone reads qaddara without gemination.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r1.anchor: قرأ الكسائي وحده قدر بالتخفيف فهدى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r2.claim: Mujāhid says God determined wretchedness and felicity and guided to right direction or error.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r2.anchor: أحدها قدر الشقاوة والسعادة وهدى للرشد والضلالة قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r3.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r3.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says God gave each animal what suits it and guided it to that provision.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r3.anchor: والثاني جعل لكل دابة ما يصلحها وهداها اليه قاله عطاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddī says God determined the fetus's term in the womb and guided it to emerge.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r4.anchor: والثالث قدر مدة الجنين في الرحم ثم هداه للخروج قاله السدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r5.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r5.claim: Muqātil says He determined them male or female and guided the male to approach the female.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r5.anchor: والرابع قدرهم ذكورا وإناثا وهدى الذكر لإتيان الأنثى قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r6.claim: Al-Zajjāj supplies an ellipsis: God determined and guided, and also led astray, omitted because the context implies it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r6.anchor: والخامس أن المعنى قدر فهدى وأضل فحذف وأضل لأن في الكلام دليلا على ذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r7.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r7.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī transmits two further views: God apportioned provisions and guided creatures to seek them, or determined sins and guided people to repentance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p88#2/r7.anchor: والسادس قدر الأرزاق وهدى إلى طلبها والسابع قدر الذنوب وهدى إلى التوبة حكاهما الثعلبي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r2.claim: God guides people toward either wretchedness or felicity and guides livestock to their grazing places.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد: هدى الإنسان للشقاوة والسعادة، وهدى الأنعام لمراتعها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r3.claim: The verse echoes Moses' statement to Pharaoh that God gave each thing its form and then guided it, and a report that God decreed creation fifty thousand years before creating the heavens and earth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r3.anchor: وهذه الآية كقوله تعالى إخبارا عن موسى أنه قال لفرعون: {ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى} [طه:5]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r4.claim: The Prophet said God decreed the destinies of creatures fifty thousand years before creating the heavens and earth, while His Throne was over water.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله ابن عمرو: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن الله قدر مقادير الخلائق

KASHSHAF:87:3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:3/r1.claim: God apportioned what benefits each animal, guided it to it, and taught it how to use it.

KASHSHAF:87:3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:3/r2.claim: A story says a thousand-year-old blind snake is inspired to seek fresh fennel, rub its eyes, and regain sight by God's leave.
KASHSHAF:87:3/r2.anchor: يحكى أنّ الأفعى إذا أتت عليها ألف سنة عميت

KASHSHAF:87:3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:3/r3.claim: Guidance to human needs in religion and worldly life, and animal and bird instincts, is too broad for any description to encompass.
KASHSHAF:87:3/r3.anchor: وهدايات الله للإنسان إلى ما لا يحدّ من مصالحه وما لا يحصر من حوائجه

KASHSHAF:87:3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:3/r4.claim: A lighter reading has qaddara; ahwa is an adjective of ghutha, meaning the pasture that He brought forth.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r5.claim: God determined what benefits each animal and guided it to recognize how to use it; this is one example of God's vast guidance of humans and other creatures.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r5.anchor: فهداه إليه وعرفه وجه الانتفاع به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r6.claim: An anecdote says a thousand-year-old blind snake finds fresh rue in a distant garden, rubs its eyes, and regains sight by God's permission.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r6.anchor: فربما كانت في برية بينها وبين الريف مسيرة أيام فتطوى تلك المسافة على طولها وعلى عماها حتى تهجم في بعض البساتين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r7.claim: God's guidance of human needs and of beasts, birds, and earth's creatures is too broad to be encompassed by description.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r7.anchor: وهدايات الله للإنسان إلى ما لا يحد من مصالحه وما لا يحصر من حوائجه في أغذيته وأدويته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r8.claim: A reading lightens the dāl in qaddara.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r13.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r13.claim: He says God decreed wretchedness and happiness and guided people to right guidance or error.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r14.claim: A second interpretation says God determined people's provisions and guided humans to livelihoods and animals to pasture.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r15.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r15.claim: He says God determined male and female and guided the male in how to approach the female.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r16.claim: One possibility is that God determined their creation in the womb and guided them to emerge fully formed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r16.anchor: قدر خلقهم في الأرحام , وهداهم الخروج للتمام

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p251/r17.claim: Another possibility is that God created people for recompense and guided them to action.

MUJAHID:v2p751#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p751#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p751#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says God decreed for each person either misery or happiness.
MUJAHID:v2p751#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد قال أما قوله ﴿ قدر ﴾ فيقول قدر للإنسان الشقاء والسعادة

MUJAHID:v2p751#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p751#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p751#2/r2.claim: Mujahid says God guided livestock to their pastures.
MUJAHID:v2p751#2/r2.anchor: وأما قوله ﴿ هدى ﴾ فيقول هدى الأنعام لمراتعها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#3/r1.claim: God allotted each animal what benefits it, guided it to that provision, and taught it how to use it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#3/r1.anchor: أى قدرلكل حيوان ما يصلحه فهداه إليه وعرفه وجه الانتفاع به

NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#3/r2.claim: Alternatively, “guided” implies both guiding and leading astray, with the latter omitted by ellipsis as in the cited verse.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#3/r2.anchor: أو فهدى وأضل ولكن حذف وأضل اكتفاء كقوله يضل من يشاء ويهدى من يشاء

QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r5.speaker: علي والسلمي والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r5.claim: ʿAli, al-Sulami, and al-Kisaʾi read qadara with a light dāl; the other readers double it, and both readings have the same meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r5.anchor: قرأ علي رضي الله عنه والسلمي والكسائي «قدر» مخففة الدال، وشدد الباقون.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r6.claim: God determined and guided each creature to its form and direction; hidaya here means directing or showing.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r6.anchor: أي قدر ووفق لكل شكل شكله. { فهدى } أي أرشد.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r7.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r7.claim: Mujahid says God determined misery and happiness and guided to rightness and error; he also says He guided humans to their destinies and cattle to pasture.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r7.anchor: قال مجاهد: قدر الشقاوة والسعادة، وهدى للرشد والضلالة.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r8.claim: Other interpreters say God determined provisions and livelihoods, then guided people in their work and animals to pasture.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r8.anchor: وقيل: قدر أقواتهم وأرزاقهم، وهداهم لمعاشهم إن كانوا إنسا، ولمراعيهم إن كانوا وحشا.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r9.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي ومقاتل والكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r9.claim: These interpreters explain fahadā as teaching creatures how to mate, as in “He gave each thing its creation, then guided it.”
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r9.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس والسدي ومقاتل والكلبي في قوله «فهدى» قالوا: عرف خلقه كيف يأتي الذكر الأنثى كما قال في طه:

QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r10.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r10.claim: ʿAta says God gave each animal what suits it and guided it toward that provision.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r10.anchor: وقال عطاء: جعل لكل دابة ما يصلحها، وهداها له.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r11.claim: One interpretation says God created benefits in things and guided people to extract them; another says He fitted each animal with what helps it and showed how to use it.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r11.anchor: وقيل: خلق المنافع في الأشياء، وهدى الإنسان لوجه استخراجها منها.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r12.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r12.claim: Al-Suddi says God determined gestation for roughly nine months, with variation, and guided the fetus to emerge from the womb.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r12.anchor: وقال السدي: قدر مدة الجنين في الرحم تسعة أشهر، وأقل وأكثر، ثم هداه للخروج من الرحم.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r13.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r13.claim: Al-Farraʾ says the verse mentions guidance while implying both guidance and misguidance, as scripture can mention one side alone.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:2-3/r13.anchor: وقال الفراء: أي قدر، فهدى وأضل فاكتفى بذكر أحدهما كقوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:87:4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:4/r1.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:87:4/r1.claim: Al-Farraʾ uses the verse about garments protecting from heat as an example of mentioning one side while omitting its opposite.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:4/r2.claim: The light-dāl reading may mean determination or, alternatively, power and dominion; God owns all things and guides whom He wills. The author’s teacher reads the preceding divine acts as indicating transcendence over creation.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:4/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون من القدرة والملك أي ملك الأشياء، وهدى من يشاء.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:4/r3.claim: “Guided” may mean called all to faith, as in God’s direction to the straight path, or that divine acts reveal His oneness, knowledge, and power.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:4/r3.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون بمعنى دعا إلى الإيمان كقوله تعالى:

NAHHAS:v5p203/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p203/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p203/r14.claim: Qaddara means that He determined their forms, provisions, and deeds.

NAHHAS:v5p203/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p203/r15.speaker: بعضهم
NAHHAS:v5p203/r15.claim: One explanation of fa-hadā is that God made matters clear to people.

NAHHAS:v5p203/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p203/r16.speaker: بعضهم
NAHHAS:v5p203/r16.claim: Another explanation is that He guided and led astray.

NAHHAS:v5p203/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p203/r17.speaker: بعضهم
NAHHAS:v5p203/r17.claim: A third explanation is that He guided them to their interests.

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.claim: Al-Aʿla is Meccan and has nineteen verses; the Prophet loved it, recited it at Eid and Friday prayers with al-Ghashiya, sometimes on the same day.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.anchor: سورة الأعلى مكية وآياتها تسع عشرة

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r2.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet loved this surah; Muslim reports that he recited it with al-Ghashiya at Eid and on Friday, sometimes reciting both on one day.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r2.anchor: أن رسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] كان يحب هذه السورة

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.claim: The surah turns the entire cosmos into a sanctuary reverberating with praise and offers the Prophet good news of divine preservation and ease in his mission and affairs.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.anchor: وحق لرسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] أن يحب هذه السورة وهي تحيل له الكون كله معبدا

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.claim: Its foundations are God's oneness as creator, divine revelation, and afterlife recompense, rooted in earlier scriptures; it also portrays the easy nature of the message, messenger, and community.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.anchor: وهي تتضمن الثابت من قواعد التصور الإيماني

QUTB-ZILAL:87:3/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:3/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:3/r1.claim: God assigns every creature its function and end, guides it to its purpose, and provides and guides it toward what sustains it throughout its life.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:3/r1.anchor: والذي قدر لكل مخلوق وظيفته وغايته

RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r1.claim: The objection that 'Great' and 'Highest' imply two gods fails because God's oneness is established and the verse never says He is higher than another lord.
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r1.anchor: هذه الآية أنه سبحانه وتعالى أعلى من رب آخر

RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r6.claim: Creation and guidance answer the implied question of why God merits glorification and form a core proof for God's existence, used by Abraham, Moses, and the first revelations to Muhammad.
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r6.anchor: فكأن سائلا قال : الاشتغال بالتسبيح إنما يكون بعد المعرفة

RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r7.claim: The proof from creation and guidance is especially compelling because its wonders are abundant and people can observe them directly.
RAZI-FULL:v31p125#2/r7.anchor: العجائب والغرائب في هذه الطريقة أكثر

RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r6.claim: Most readers use the doubled form qaddara, meaning God assigned each thing a known measure; al-Kisa'i reads the lighter form.
RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r6.anchor: قرأ الجمهور : { قدر } مشددة وقرأ الكسائي على التخفيف

RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r7.claim: For the lighter reading, al-Qaffal explains qadara as 'owned and governed': God owns what He creates and guides it to its interests; others regard the readings as synonymous.
RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r7.anchor: فقال القفال : معناه ملك فهدى وتأويله : أنه خلق فسوى

RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r8.claim: God measured every created entity in its body, lifespan, qualities, appearance, properties, circumstances, and fate, including guidance and misguidance.
RAZI-FULL:v31p126/r8.anchor: قدر السموات والكواكب والعناصر والمعادن والنبات والحيوان والإنسان بمقدار مخصوص

RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r1.claim: Proportioning arranges bodily elements so each is ready for a particular capacity, and guidance creates those capacities in the organs so their actions together serve complete welfare.
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r1.anchor: عبارة عن خلق تلك القوى في تلك الأعضاء

RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r2.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r2.claim: Muqatil says God guided the male to the female and taught him how to approach her.
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل : هدى الذكر للأنثى كيف يأتيها

RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r3.claim: Other interpreters say God guides creatures to their livelihood and cares for them.

RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r4.claim: Other interpreters say God guides people to good and evil and to happiness or misery by giving them perception and the ability to act or refrain.
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r4.anchor: هدى الإنسان لسبل الخير والشر والسعادة والشقاوة

RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r5.speaker: السدي
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says God determined the fetus's time in the womb and guided it out at birth.
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r5.anchor: وقال السدي : قدر مدة الجنين في الرحم ثم هداه للخروج

RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r6.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r6.claim: Al-Farra says 'guided' also implies 'led astray,' with one opposite omitted, as another verse mentions protection from heat without naming cold.
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r6.anchor: وقال الفراء : قدر فهدى وأضل ، فاكتفى بذكر إحداهما

RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r7.claim: Some interpreters take guidance as calling people to faith, to which all were invited.
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون : الهداية بمعنى الدعاء إلى الإيمان

RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r8.claim: Another view says the ordered, perfected acts visible in the world guide rational observers to God's oneness, majesty, and unique self-sufficiency.
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r8.anchor: هدى أي دلهم بأفعاله على توحيده وجلال كبريائه

RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r9.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r9.claim: Qatada says God does not compel or command misguidance or sin, nor approve it; He approves and commands obedience and forbids sin.
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة في قوله : { فهدى } إن الله تعالى ما أكره عبدا

RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r10.claim: The reported meanings fall into guidance for worldly interests or religious life; the author prefers the religious sense because creation and measuring already cover worldly constitution and capacities.
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r10.anchor: والأول أقوى ، لأن قوله : { خلق فسوى * وقدر } يرجع إلى أحوال الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r11.claim: On the preferred reading, God completes human reason and powers, then charges people with religious duties and directs them to faith.
RAZI-FULL:v31p127/r11.anchor: ثم أتبعه بقوله : { فهدى } أي كلفه ودله على الدين

SAMIN-DURR:87:3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:87:3/r1.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads qaddara with a light dāl; the other readers double it, and both readings appeared earlier in al-Mursalāt.
SAMIN-DURR:87:3/r1.anchor: قرأ الكسائي بتخفيف الدال، والباقون بالتشديد.

STUDYQURAN:87:2/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r1.claim: Created can refer specifically to humans, to humans and animals, or to all creation.
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r1.anchor: Here created refers to human beings in particular, to human beings and animals, or to all of creation

STUDYQURAN:87:2/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r2.claim: On the human-specific reading, God fashioned the first human after breathing His Spirit into him, without irregularity, then measured his form and provided nourishment.
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r2.anchor: God fashioned the first human being after breathing into him of His Spirit, leaving him without irregularities

STUDYQURAN:87:2/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r3.claim: Qaddara can also be read qadara, meaning to have power or determine, so God retains direct power over all He created.
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r3.anchor: Measured out renders qaddara, which can also be read qadara, meaning to have power or to determine

STUDYQURAN:87:2/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r4.claim: Guidance may be the instinct by which creatures seek their allotted nourishment, or God’s leading people to religion and knowledge of Unity through signs and proofs.
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r4.anchor: Here guidance refers to the instinct God puts in all things to be able to seek the nourishment that He has already measured out for them

STUDYQURAN:87:2/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r5.claim: The broader implication is that creation is properly formed without imperfection or flaw.
STUDYQURAN:87:2/r5.anchor: The broader implication is that creation is as it should be, without imperfection or flaw

TAB-FULL:v24p312/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p312/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p312/r1.claim: Mujāhid says God guides humans toward wretchedness or happiness and livestock to their grazing places.
TAB-FULL:v24p312/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: " {قدر فهدى} [الأعلى: 3] قال: هدى الإنسان للشقوة والسعادة، وهدى الأنعام لمراتعها

TAB-FULL:v24p312/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p312/r2.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p312/r2.claim: Others interpret the guidance as directing males to the mating place of females.
TAB-FULL:v24p312/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل معنى ذلك: هدى الذكور لمأتى الإناث.

TAB-FULL:v24p312/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p312/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p312/r3.claim: Ṭabarī takes the statement generally: God guides all creatures, including along the paths of good and evil and males to females, absent proof restricting its scope.
TAB-FULL:v24p312/r3.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك عندنا: أن الله عم بقوله {فهدى} [الأعلى: 3] الخبر عن هدايته خلقه

TAB-FULL:v24p312/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p312/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p312/r4.claim: Most regional readers intensify the dāl in qaddara; al-Kisāʾī lightens it, but the intensified reading is preferred by consensus.
TAB-FULL:v24p312/r4.anchor: واجتمعت قراء الأمصار على تشديد الدال من قدر، غير الكسائي فإنه خففها.

TABATABAI:87:17-19/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r7.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r7.claim: Al-Qummī says God first determined things by an initial measure, then guided whom He wills to them.
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r7.anchor: قال قدر الأشياء بالتقدير الأول ثم هدى إليها من يشاء

ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r3.claim: God guided the way, whether the person proves grateful or ungrateful.
ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r3.anchor: هداه السبيل إما شاكرا وإما كفورا

ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r4.speaker: بعض النحويين
ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r4.claim: Some grammarians say the phrase means He guided and led astray, with led astray omitted because the context supplies it, as in 14:4.
ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r4.anchor: وقال بعض النحويين: فهدى وأضل ولكن حذفت وأضل لأن في الكلام دليلا عليه،

TABRISI:87:7-9/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7-9/r1.speaker: الكسائي
TABRISI:87:7-9/r1.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads qaddara lightly; the other readers double the consonant, with both forms carrying the same sense.
TABRISI:87:7-9/r1.anchor: قرأ الكسائي قدر بالتخفيف وهو قراءة علي ع والباقون قدر بالتشديد

TABRISI:87:7-9/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7-9/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7-9/r3.claim: The light and doubled readings of qaddara are both sound because qaddara here means qaddara.
TABRISI:87:7-9/r3.anchor: قد تقدم أن قدر في معنى قدر فكلا الوجهين حسن

TABRISI:87:7/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7/r9.claim: God allotted creatures their forms and means of livelihood, then guided them to monotheism through signs and proofs.
TABRISI:87:7/r9.anchor: قدر الخلق على ما خلقهم فيه من الصور والهيئات وأجرى لهم أسباب معايشهم

TABRISI:87:7/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7/r10.claim: Another interpretation says God allotted their provisions and guided them to seek them.

TABRISI:87:7/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7/r11.claim: God may have determined creatures according to wisdom and guided each animal to what benefits or harms it, even a baby to its mother's breast.
TABRISI:87:7/r11.anchor: أرشد كل حيوان إلى ما فيه منفعته ومضرته حتى أنه سبحانه هدى الطفل إلى ثدي أمه

TABRISI:87:7/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7/r12.speaker: مقاتل، الكلبي
TABRISI:87:7/r12.claim: Maqātil and al-Kalbī interpret this as assigning male and female forms and guiding the male to the female.
TABRISI:87:7/r12.anchor: قدرهم ذكورا وإناثا وهدى الذكر كيف يأتي الأنثى عن مقاتل والكلبي

TABRISI:87:7/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7/r13.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:87:7/r13.claim: Mujāhid says God guided creatures to the path of good and evil.
TABRISI:87:7/r13.anchor: هدى إلى سبيل الخير والشر عن مجاهد

TABRISI:87:7/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7/r14.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:87:7/r14.claim: Al-Suddī says God determines the fetus's gestation and guides it to emerge when complete.
TABRISI:87:7/r14.anchor: قدر الولد في البطن تسعة أشهر أو أقل أو أكثر وهدى للخروج منه للتمام عن السدي

TABRISI:87:7/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7/r15.claim: Another explanation says God placed benefits in things and guided people to extract and use them as food, medicine, or poison.
TABRISI:87:7/r15.anchor: قدر المنافع في الأشياء وهدى الإنسان لاستخراجها منه فجعل بعضها غذاء وبعضها دواء وبعضها سما

THALABI:v10p183#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p183#2/r8.speaker: علي
THALABI:v10p183#2/r8.claim: ʿAlī, al-Sulamī, and al-Kisāʾī read qaddara with a light dāl; the other readers geminate it.
THALABI:v10p183#2/r8.anchor:
خفف علي والسلمي والكسائي داله
، وشددها الآخرون

THALABI:v10p183#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p183#2/r9.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v10p183#2/r9.claim: Mujāhid says God guided humanity to good and evil, felicity and misery, and livestock to their grazing places.
THALABI:v10p183#2/r9.anchor: قال مجاهد: هدى الإنسان لسبيل الخير والشر والسعادة والشقاوة وهدى الأنعام لمراتعها

THALABI:v10p183#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p183#2/r10.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
THALABI:v10p183#2/r10.claim: Muqātil and al-Kalbī say God taught creatures how the male approaches the female.
THALABI:v10p183#2/r10.anchor: وقال مقاتل والكلبي: عرف خلقه كيف يأتي الذكر الأنثى

THALABI:v10p183#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p183#2/r11.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v10p183#2/r11.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says every animal was given what suits and sustains it.
THALABI:v10p183#2/r11.anchor:
وعن عطاء قال:
جعل لكل دابة ما يصلحها

THALABI:v10p183#2/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p183#2/r12.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v10p183#2/r12.claim: Other glosses say God guided creatures to acquire provisions and livelihood, or made useful things and taught people how to extract their benefits, or guided whom He wills to religion.
THALABI:v10p183#2/r12.anchor: وقيل: هدى لاكتساب الأرزاق والمعاش، وقيل: خلق المنافع في الأشياء

THALABI:v10p183#2/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p183#2/r13.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v10p183#2/r13.claim: Al-Suddī says God set gestation in the womb for nine months, shorter or longer, and guided the child to emerge.
THALABI:v10p183#2/r13.anchor: قال السدي: قدر الولد في الرحم تسعة أشهر، أقل، أو أكثر، وهدى للخروج من الرحم

THALABI:v10p183#2/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p183#2/r14.speaker: الواسطي
THALABI:v10p183#2/r14.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī says God decreed felicity or misery and made each person follow what was decreed for him.
THALABI:v10p183#2/r14.anchor: وقال الواسطي: قدر السعادة والشقاوة عليهم ثم يسر لكل واحد من الطالعين سلوك ما قدر عليه

THALABI:v10p183#2/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p183#2/r15.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v10p183#2/r15.claim: Other explanations say God apportioned provisions and guided their pursuit, or decreed sins and then guided people to repentance.
THALABI:v10p183#2/r15.anchor: وقيل: قدر الأرزاق فهداهم لطلبها، وقيل: قدر الذنوب على عباده ثم هداهم الى التوبة

ASAD-NOTES:87:1#n2/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:87:1#n2/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:87:1#n2/r1.claim: Asad links God's determining and guiding to the closing sentence of 25:2 and to 20:50.
ASAD-NOTES:87:1#n2/r1.anchor: Cf. the last sentence of 25:2 and the corresponding note 3; also 20:50

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r4.claim: The lightened and unlightened readings of “qaddara” have the same meaning.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r5.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r5.claim: God determined the offspring He willed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r5.anchor: قال عطاء: قدر من النسل ما أراد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r6.claim: God determined the male and female forms of animals.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل: قدر خلق الذكر # والأنثى من الدواب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس، الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r7.claim: God guided male and female animals in how to mate.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r7.anchor: {فهدى}. الذكر، والأنثى كيف يأتيها، وهو قول ابن عباس (¬2)، (والكلبي)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r8.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r8.claim: The guidance resembles the verse saying God gave each thing its form and then guided it, referring here to male and female animals.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r8.anchor: عطاء: مثل قوله: {أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى} (¬5) يريد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r9.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r9.claim: The preferred explanation is that God guides each male animal to mate with a female of its own kind; mating differs by species, so God gives each male that knowledge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r9.anchor: صاحب النظم، قال: معنى هذا (¬7) هداية الذكر لإتيان الأنثى كيف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r10.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r10.claim: An alternative is that God guided creatures to their livelihood and pasture.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r10.anchor: وذكر مقاتل قولا آخر فقال: هداه لمعيشته ومرعاه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r11.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r11.claim: God guided humanity to good and evil, felicity and misery.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r11.anchor:
وقال مجاهد:
هدى الإنسان لسبيل الخير، والشر، والسعادة (¬1)، والشقاوة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r12.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r12.claim: God determined the fetus’s time in the womb, then guided it to emerge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r12.anchor: وقال السدي: قدر مدة الجنين في الرحم، ثم هدى للخروج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r13.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r13.claim: The phrase implies both guidance and misguidance, mentioning guidance alone because it commonly accompanies misguidance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p431#2/r13.anchor: وقال الفراء: قدر فهدى وأضل، واكتفى من ذكر الضلال بالهدى

WAHIDI-QT:87:3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:87:3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:87:3/r1.claim: God apportioned provisions and then guided creatures to seek them.

ELMALILI:87:3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:3/r1.claim: God assigns every created thing a measured limit by knowledge and will, specifying kinds, individuals, qualities, acts, and lifespans, as 65:3 states.
ELMALILI:87:3/r1.anchor: ilm ü iradesiyle bir kader tâyin eyledi: Cinslerinde

ELMALILI:87:3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:3/r2.claim: His determination differentiates otherwise equally possible things into distinct natures and identities, assigning forms and characteristics, whether innate or chosen.
ELMALILI:87:3/r2.anchor: Cinslerinde, nevilerinde ferdlerinde, sıfatlarında, fiillerinde, ecellerinde

ELMALILI:87:3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:3/r3.claim: He guides each creature toward its created end through capacities, inclinations, inspirations, proofs, and revealed signs, bringing it from beginning toward its worldly and otherworldly outcome.
ELMALILI:87:3/r3.anchor: mâ-hulika-lehleri olan mikdâra müyesser kılmak üzere yoluna koydu

ELMALILI:87:3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:3/r4.claim: Humans receive guidance through reason and religion; Muhammad was specifically destined for prophethood and granted guidance and success.
ELMALILI:87:3/r4.anchor: insana da akıl ve din hidâyetleriyle kendini ve yolunu göstermekte

ELMALILI:87:3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:3/r5.claim: Study of celestial motion and the states of matter, plants, and animals reveals astonishing divine knowledge, power, governance, and guidance; human inward and outward guidance, especially reason and religion, is higher still.
ELMALILI:87:3/r5.anchor: ne kadar derin, ne kadar ince, ne kadar büyük ilm ü kudret ile idare ve hidâyet tecelliyâtı görülür

ELMALILI:87:3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:3/r6.claim: All created capacities and measures are finite; no creature has unlimited total power, while the Determiner, Guide, Knower, and Powerful Lord transcends them.
ELMALILI:87:3/r6.anchor: Hepsi kemmiyet kanunlarının hükmü altında mekādîr-i mahsûsa ile mahduddur

ELMALILI:87:3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:3/r7.claim: Some restrict guidance to human reason, religion, and prophetic direction; others take it as instinctive life needs, provisions, and uses for living creatures.
ELMALILI:87:3/r7.anchor: Bazıları burada “hidâyet”i akıl ve din hidâyeti gibi insana mahsus olan hidâyet

ELMALILI:87:3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:3/r8.claim: Elmalılı prefers the unrestricted reading: human and prophetic guidance is the highest example, but the apparent sense includes every entity being directed naturally or voluntarily toward its goal, as in 20:50.
ELMALILI:87:3/r8.anchor: doğrusu insanlara mahsus olan ve bilhassa Resûlullah’a ait bulunan hidâyet ve irşad bunun en yüksek misâl

ELMALILI:87:3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:3/r9.claim: This universal guidance includes planetary orbits, attraction, gas expansion and contraction, falling stones, crystallization, dissolving salt, burning coal, and cellular processes.
ELMALILI:87:3/r9.anchor: bir kürenin diğerine doğru mihver veya mahrekinde devri, bir cüz’ün diğer bir cüz’e incizâbı

ELMALILI:87:3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:3/r10.claim: Determination covers every entity's essence and properties: size, duration, qualities, colors, tastes, states, beauty, happiness, guidance, and misguidance, throughout all worlds.
ELMALILI:87:3/r10.anchor: Semâvât ve Arz, kevâkib ve anâsır, me‘âdin, nebâtât, hayvânât ve insanlardan her birine

ELMALILI:87:3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:3/r11.claim: God sends everything down according to a known measure, as 15:21 says; the scope is too vast to detail exhaustively, and the secret of destiny is not fully known to us beforehand.
ELMALILI:87:3/r11.anchor: bir kader-i ma‘lûm ve bir kader-i mahsus ile tahdid ve tahsis eylemiştir

ELMALILI:87:3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:3/r12.claim: Although possible nature could receive many forms, the Creator assigns each actual entity a particular temperament and capacity; each capacity is suited to certain acts, and its direction toward its end is specific guidance.
ELMALILI:87:3/r12.anchor: Hâlık’ın takdir ve tahsîsi ile vücudda her mizac bir kuvve-i hâssaya müsta‘id kılınmıştır

ELMALILI:87:3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:3/r13.claim: The Lord's power rises above every limited creature, so His highest name is free of their defects and believers should trust His command and planning to overcome the disbelievers' schemes.
ELMALILI:87:3/r13.anchor: O’nun ism-i a‘lâsı bütün bunlardaki mahdûdiyet ve noksan şâibelerinden tenzih olunmalı

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:2-5:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:2-5:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:2-5:anmerkung/r1.claim: The perfects are aspectual rather than inherently past; verses 4–5 show creation as ongoing world-sustaining activity through the pasture’s recurring growth and decay.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:2-5:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Dass Gottes Schöpfungstätigkeit hier nicht als einmaliger Akt, sondern als fortwährende, welterhaltende Aktivität verstanden wird

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:3:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:3:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:3:anmerkung/r1.claim: The note links qaddara to Q 80:19 and hadā/hudā to the discussion of Q 93:7.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:3:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zu qaddara vgl. 80:19, zu hadā bzw. hudā s. die Anmerkung zu 93:7

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r3.claim: God’s guidance of creation means determining its nature and directing it toward its purpose and wisdom.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r3.anchor: yarattığı şeylerin tabiatını belirleyip onu yaratılış gayesine, hikmet ve hedefine doğru yöneltmesidir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r4.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r4.claim: Shawkani says God determines creatures’ kinds, traits, actions, speech, and lifespans, then guides and enables each toward its purpose and proper religious and worldly conduct.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r4.anchor: Şevkânî âyeti şöyle yorumlar: “Allah varlıkların cinslerini, türlerini, niteliklerini, ne yapacaklarını, ne söyleyeceklerini ve nihayet ecellerini takdir etmiştir

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p369/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p369/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p369/r1.claim: The fragment explains the divine guidance as determining the male and female and guiding them to intercourse.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p369/r1.anchor:
قعيدا وقيل قدر
 الذكر للانثى وهداه لاتيانها

IBNMUJAHID:v1p680/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p680/r1.speaker: الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p680/r1.claim: Al-Kisāʾī alone reads قدر with a light dāl; the other readers double it.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p680/r1.anchor: قرأ الكسائى وحده ﴿ قدر ﴾ خفيفة وقرأ الباقون ﴿ قدر ﴾ مشددة

QIRAAT-ER:87:3:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:87:3:3#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:87:3:3#1/r1.claim: Form I qadara without shadda permits the senses measuring, determining, estimating, or having ability, beside intensive Form II qaddara.
QIRAAT-ER:87:3:3#1/r1.anchor: Form I qadara allows simple measuring, determining, estimating, or ability, beside intensive Form II qaddara

ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r1.claim: Alusi's preferred reading is that God assigned exact measures to kinds, species, individuals, traits, acts, and lifespans, then guided each creature toward its natural or chosen outcome through inclinations, inspiration, signs, and revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r1.anchor: جعل الأشياء على مقادير مخصوصة في أجناسها وأنواعها وأفرادها وصفاتها وأفعالها وآجالها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r2.claim: The varieties of guidance are extraordinary in plants and animals and still greater in humans, beyond the reach of description or compilation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r2.anchor: وأما فنون هداياته سبحانه وتعالى للأنسان على الخصوص ففوق ذلك بمراحل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r3.claim: Other views say God shaped each creature, provided its livelihood, and guided it to religion and knowledge of divine unity; or assigned provisions and directed creatures to seek them.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r3.anchor: وقيل أي والذي قدر الخلق على ما خلقهم فيه من الصور والهيئات وأجرى لهم أسباب معاشهم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r4.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r4.claim: Muqatil and al-Kalbi say God determined creatures as male and female and guided the male in approaching the female.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r4.anchor: وعن مقاتل والكلبي قدرهم ذكرانا وإناثا وهدى الذكر كيف يأتي الأنثى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r5.claim: Mujahid says God measured humans and animals, guiding humans to good and evil and animals to grazing places.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r5.anchor: وعن مجاهد قدر الإنسان والبهائم وهدى الإنسان للخير والشر والبهائم للمراتع

ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r6.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r6.claim: Al-Suddi says God set the fetus's time in the womb at nine months, less, or more, and guided it to emerge fully formed.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r6.anchor: وعن السدي قدر الولد في البطن تسعة أشهر أو أقل أو أكثر وهداه للخروج منه للتمام

ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r7.claim: Another interpretation says God placed benefits in things and guided people to extract them; Alusi treats such specifications as examples of his broader reading, not limits on it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r7.anchor: وقيل قدر المنافع في الأشياء وهدى الإنسان لاستخراجها والأولى ما ذكر أولا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r8.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r8.claim: Al-Farraʾ claims the verse omits “and misled”; Alusi rejects this proposed ellipsis.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r8.anchor: وزعم الفراء في الآية اكتفاء والأصل فهدى وأضل وليس بشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r9.speaker: الكسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r9.claim: Al-Kisaʾi reads qaddara with a light dāl, from ability or measuring.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104/r9.anchor: وقرأالكسائي قدر بالتخفيف من القدرة أو التقدير

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r3.speaker: الكسائي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r3.claim: Al-Kisaʾi reads qaddara with a light dāl; the other readers geminate it, and both forms mean the same.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r4.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r4.claim: Mujahid says God guided humans to good and evil and to felicity or misery, and guided livestock to their pastures.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هدى الإنسان لسبيل الخير والشر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r5.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r5.claim: Muqatil and al-Kalbi say God assigned every thing its course and showed animals how to mate.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r5.anchor: وقال مقاتل والكلبي: قدر لكل شيء مسلكه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r6.claim: Another view says God apportioned provisions and guided creatures to earn their livelihood.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r6.anchor: وقيل: قدر الأرزاق وهدى لاكتساب الأرزاق والمعاش

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r7.claim: Another view says God created benefits in things and guided people to discover how to extract them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r7.anchor: وقيل: خلق المنافع في الأشياء، وهدى الإنسان لوجه استخراجها منها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r8.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says God determined the embryo’s term in the womb and then guided it out.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r8.anchor: وقال السدي: قدر مدة الجنين في الرحم ثم هداه للخروج من الرحم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r9.speaker: الواسطي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r9.claim: Al-Wasiti says God predetermined bliss and misery, then made each group follow the path assigned to it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400/r9.anchor: قال الواسطي: قدر السعادة والشقاوة عليهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:1-3/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:1-3/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:1-3/r5.claim: God determined kinds, species, individuals, measures, qualities, acts, and lifespans, then directed each toward its natural or chosen acts through inclinations, inspiration, signs, and revealed verses.
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:1-3/r5.anchor: قدر أجناس الأشياء وأنواعها وأشخاصها ومقاديرها وصفاتها وأفعالها وآجالها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p395/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395/r1.claim: After mentioning the servants' schemes, the surah commands the Prophet to declare God free of their foul claims; the account of creation and guidance then displays divine power and wisdom and exposes their error.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395/r1.anchor: وكان وقوع ذلك من العبيد المحاط بأعمالهم ودقائق أنفاسهم وأحوالهم من أقبح مرتكب وأبعده عن المعرفة بشيء من عظيم أمر الخالق

BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r1.claim: God creates and proportionately forms; He assigns each thing its kinds, individuals, measures, qualities, actions and lifespans, fitting striking to the hand, walking to the leg, hearing to the ear and sight to the eye.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r1.anchor: أي أوقع تقديره في أجناس الأشياء وأنواعها وأشخاصها ومقاديرها وصفاتها وأفعالها وآجالها , وغير ذلك من أحوالها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r2.claim: God's guidance follows His apportionment by fitting substances, forms and properties to natural or chosen purposes, creating inclinations and inspirations and setting signs to repel harm and bring benefit; even newborns seek milk instinctively.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r2.anchor: فهدى } أي أوقع بسبب تقديره وعقبه الهداية لذلك الذي وقع التقدير من أجله من الشكل والجواهر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r3.claim: Creation requires proportion to achieve balance, and apportionment requires guidance to achieve completeness.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r3.anchor: فالخالق لا بد له من التسوية ليحصل الاعتدال , والتقدير لا بد له من الهداية ليحصل الكمال

DURR-FULL:v8p481/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p481/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v8p481/r1.claim: After the Companions asked what to say in prostration, the sūra was revealed and the Prophet instructed them to say “Glory to my Lord, the Most High.”
DURR-FULL:v8p481/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قلنا يا رسول الله كيف نقول في سجودنا فأنزل الله

DURR-FULL:v8p481/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p481/r2.speaker: حضرمى بن عامر
DURR-FULL:v8p481/r2.claim: When Ḥaḍramī recited the verses and added his own line about the pregnant woman, the Prophet told him to add no more, calling the recitation sufficient.
DURR-FULL:v8p481/r2.anchor: عن الكلبي قال: وفد حضرمي بن عامر على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

TAB:87:3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:3/r1.speaker: author
TAB:87:3/r1.claim: God determined His creation and guided it.

TAB:87:3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:87:3/r2.claim: Mujahid says God guided humans to misery or happiness and livestock to their pastures.
TAB:87:3/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد ، قوله : قَدّرَ فَهَدَى قال : هدى الإنسان للشّقوة والسعادة

TAB:87:3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:3/r3.speaker: آخرون
TAB:87:3/r3.claim: Another view specifies that God guided males to the place where they mate with females.
TAB:87:3/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل معنى ذلك : هدى الذكور لمأتى الإناث

TAB:87:3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:3/r4.speaker: author
TAB:87:3/r4.claim: Al-Tabari keeps the guidance general: God guided creation to good and evil and guided males to females, absent proof restricting the verse to one sense.
TAB:87:3/r4.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك عندنا : أن الله عمّ بقوله فَهَدَى الخبر عن هدايته خلقه ، ولم يخصص من ذلك معنى دون معنى

TAB:87:3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:3/r5.speaker: الكسائي
TAB:87:3/r5.claim: Most regional readers geminate the dāl in qaddara, while al-Kisaʾi reads it lightly; al-Tabari prefers the geminated reading by consensus.
TAB:87:3/r5.anchor: واجتمعت قرّاء الأمصار على تشديد الدال من قَدّر ، غير الكسائي فإنه خفّفها

TABATABAI:2:21-25#19/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25#19/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:21-25#19/r4.claim: Verses on divine measure show things descending from undetermined plenitude into particular existence by a determination that precedes and accompanies them, including their relations to other existents.
TABATABAI:2:21-25#19/r4.anchor: تدل على أن الأشياء تنزل من ساحة الإطلاق إلى مرحلة التعين والتشخص بتقدير منه تعالى

BURHAN:v2p446/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p446/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p446/r1.claim: One referent may take successive adjectives without conjunction, as in 68:10, or with conjunction, as in 87:1–3; their meanings should differ.
BURHAN:v2p446/r1.anchor: إذا تكررت النعوت لواحدة فتارة يترك العطف

BURHAN:v2p446/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p446/r2.speaker: الزمخشري وأبو البقاء
BURHAN:v2p446/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari and Abu al-Baqa say that conjunction signals that each adjective is an independent attribute.
BURHAN:v2p446/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري وأبو البقاء دخول العاطف يؤذن بأن كل صفة مستقله

BURHAN:v2p446/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p446/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p446/r3.claim: Conjunction is preferable when the attributes differ widely in meaning; otherwise it can be omitted.
BURHAN:v2p446/r3.anchor: والعطف أحسن إن تباعد معنى الصفات

RUMMANI:v1p101/r1.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p101/r1.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p101/r1.claim: Rummānī defines taṣrīf as expressing one meaning through varied related meanings and indications, linked successively, like derivation from a root.
RUMMANI:v1p101/r1.anchor: التصريف تصريف المعنى في المعاني المختلفة , كتصريفه في الدلالات المختلفة , وهو عقدها به على جهة التعاقب

RUMMANI:v1p101/r2.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p101/r2.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p101/r2.claim: He illustrates semantic taṣrīf through forms from ملك, including owner, king, possessor of sovereignty, and forms for giving, sharing, and possessing dominion.
RUMMANI:v1p101/r2.anchor: فصرف في معنى مالك , وملك , ذي الملكوت , والمليك , وفي معنى التمليك , والتمالك , والإملاك

RUMMANI:v1p101/r3.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p101/r3.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p101/r3.claim: The many derivatives of عرض, from appearing and turning away to objection, display, opposition, transient appearance, and poetic meter, all center on appearance.
RUMMANI:v1p101/r3.anchor: كله منعقد بمعنى الظهور. ومنه: أعرضت اليمامة أي ظهرت وهو الأصل , ومنه أيضا الإعراض عن الإنسان لأنه انزواء عن الظهور له

RUMMANI:v1p101/r4.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p101/r4.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p101/r4.claim: This kind of taṣrīf clarifies a meaning strikingly by surrounding it with related meanings that reveal and indicate it.
RUMMANI:v1p101/r4.anchor: وهذا الضرب من التصريف فيه بيان عجيب يظهر فيه المعنى بما يكتنفه من المعاني التي تظهره وتدل عليه

RUMMANI:v1p101/r5.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p101/r5.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p101/r5.claim: The Qur'an varies the account of Moses across al-Aʿrāf, Ṭā Hā, al-Shuʿarāʾ, and other sūras for several purposes.
RUMMANI:v1p101/r5.anchor: أما تصريف المعنى في الدلالات المختلفة فقد جاء في القرآن في غير قصة , منها قصة موسى عليه السلام , ذكرت في سورة الأعراف وفي طه والشعراء

RUMMANI:v1p101/r6.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p101/r6.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p101/r6.claim: One wisdom of retelling Moses' story in varied forms is preserving the highest level of eloquence without diminishing it.
RUMMANI:v1p101/r6.anchor: منها التصرف في البلاغة من غير نقصان عن أعلى مرتبة

RUMMANI:v1p101/r7.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p101/r7.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p101/r7.claim: Another purpose of varying the narrative is to strengthen its lesson and admonition.

RUMMANI:v1p101/r8.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p101/r8.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p101/r8.claim: A further purpose is to resolve doubts concerning the miracle.

RUMMANI:v1p101/r9.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p101/r9.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p101/r9.claim: He distinguishes challenges outside what is possible from those within it: arithmetic relations such as five times five equaling twenty-five or the unique square root of one hundred cannot sensibly be challenged otherwise.
RUMMANI:v1p101/r9.anchor: فالأول كالتحدي بعدد يضرب في عدد فيكون منه خمسة وعشرون غير خمسة في خمسة

RUMMANI:v1p101/r10.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p101/r10.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p101/r10.claim: Unlike such constrained cases, the highest eloquence lies within God's power: He can produce whatever resembles the Qur'an, so expressing one meaning in varied, highest-level forms demonstrates the challenge to disbelievers.
RUMMANI:v1p101/r10.anchor: وليس كذلك سبيل أعلى الطبقات في البلاغة لأن الذي قدر على أن يأتي بسورة آل عمران والذي قدر على المائدة هو الذي قدر على الإنعام

DAMGHANI:v1p371/r11.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p371/r11.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p371/r11.claim: Qaddara can mean to shape or form; the source glosses God’s act as shaping well in the womb and guiding.
DAMGHANI:v1p371/r11.anchor: الرابع قدر وقدر وصور قوله سبحانه في سورة المرسلات

DAMGHANI:v1p371/r12.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p371/r12.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p371/r12.claim: The entry also lists qaddara in the sense of making or appointing, but its explanation is cut off here.
DAMGHANI:v1p371/r12.anchor: الخامس قدر أي جعل قوله تعالى في

DAMGHANI:v1p371/r13.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p371/r13.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p371/r13.claim: The entry lists knowledge as a further sense of qaddara, without an example in this excerpt.
DAMGHANI:v1p371/r13.anchor: على ستة أوجه القدر العظمة قدر قتر قدر قوي قدر وقدر وصور قدر جعل قدر علم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248/r5.claim: In the other verse, God guides the male by inspiration to approach the female.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248/r5.anchor: والذي قدر فهدى (3) [الأعلى: 3] ، أي هدى الذكر

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p248/r8.claim: The various senses of guidance are related to one another.

NASHR:v2p399#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p399#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p399#2/r1.claim: Imāla of the rhyme endings from al-Aʿlā through Mūsā was covered earlier in the chapter on imāla.
NASHR:v2p399#2/r1.anchor: تقدم إمالة رءوس آيها من لدن الأعلى إلى وموسى في باب الإمالة

NASHR:v2p399#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p399#2/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p399#2/r2.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads قدر with a light dāl; the other readers use a geminated dāl.
NASHR:v2p399#2/r2.anchor: قرأ الكسائي قدر بتخفيف الدال وقرأ الباقون بتشديدها

ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r1.claim: The majority read qaddara with a doubled dāl; the author allows either ordaining and decreeing or measuring and balancing things.
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { قدر } بشد الدال ، فاحتمل أن يكون من القدر والقضاء ، واحتمل أن يكون من التقدير والموازنة بين الأشياء

ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says God apportioned what benefits each animal, guided it to that provision, and taught it how to use it.
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : قدّر لكل حيوان ما يصلحه ، فهداه إليه وعرّفه وجه الانتفاع به ، انتهى .

ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r3.speaker: الكسائي
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r3.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads with a light dāl, deriving the form from power or from measurement and balancing.
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r3.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي : قدر مخفف الدال من القدرة أو من التقدير والموازنة ، وهدى عام لجميع الهدايات .

ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r4.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes the guidance to imply its counterpart, misguidance: “He guided and led astray.”
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r4.anchor: وقال الفرّاء : فهدى وأضل ، اكتفى بالواحدة عن الأخرى .

ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r5.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r5.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil say God guided animals to mate, directing males to females.
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r5.anchor: وقال الكلبي ومقاتل : هدى الحيوان إلى وطء الذكور للإناث .

ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r6.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r6.claim: Mujāhid says humans are guided to good and evil, while beasts are guided to grazing places.
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد : هدى الإنسان للخير والشر ، والبهائم للمراتع .

ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r7.claim: Another example is the newborn’s guidance to suckle at the breast.
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r7.anchor: وقيل : هدى المولود عند وضعه إلى مص الثدي ، وهذه الأقوال محمولة

ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r8.claim: These examples illustrate the general guidance and do not restrict it to one kind.
ABUHAYYAN:87:3/r8.anchor: وهذه الأقوال محمولة على التمثيل لا على التخصيص .

ALUSI:87:3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:3/r1.claim: God assigned every thing specific measures across its genus, kind, individual, qualities, actions, and lifespan.
ALUSI:87:3/r1.anchor: أي جعل الأشياء على مقادير مخصوصة في أجناسها وأنواعها وأفرادها وصفاتها وأفعالها وآجالها

ALUSI:87:3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:3/r2.claim: He directed each thing to its natural or chosen function and made it apt for its purpose through inclinations, inspirations, signs, and revealed verses.
ALUSI:87:3/r2.anchor: فوجه كل واحد منها إلى ما يصدر عنه وينبغي له طبعاً أو اختياراً ويسره لما خلق له بخلق الميول والإلهامات ونصب الدلائل وإنزال الآيات

ALUSI:87:3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:3/r3.claim: Observation of plants and animals reveals guidance beyond reason’s grasp; human forms of divine guidance exceed these by far, beyond verbal description.
ALUSI:87:3/r3.anchor: فلو تتبعت أحوال النباتات والحيوانات لرأيت في كل منها ما تحار فيه العقول وتضيق عنه دفاتر النقول

ALUSI:87:3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:3/r4.claim: A reported interpretation says God fixed creatures in their forms, arranged their livelihoods, and guided them to religion and recognition of divine unity through signs.
ALUSI:87:3/r4.anchor: وقيل أي والذي قدر الخلق على ما خلقهم فيه من الصور والهيئات وأجرى لهم أسباب معاشهم من الأرزاق والأقوات

ALUSI:87:3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:3/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:87:3/r5.claim: Another view takes “measured” as assigning provisions and “guided” as directing creatures to seek them.

ALUSI:87:3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:3/r6.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
ALUSI:87:3/r6.claim: Muqātil and al-Kalbī say God made humans male and female and guided the male in approaching the female.
ALUSI:87:3/r6.anchor: وعن مقاتل والكلبي قدرهم ذكراناً وإناثاً وهدى الذكر كيف يأتي الأنثى

ALUSI:87:3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:3/r7.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI:87:3/r7.claim: Mujāhid says God measured humans and beasts, guiding humans to good and evil and beasts to their grazing places.
ALUSI:87:3/r7.anchor: وعن مجاهد قدر الإنسان والبهائم وهدى الإنسان للخير والشر والبهائم للمراتع

ALUSI:87:3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:3/r8.speaker: السدي
ALUSI:87:3/r8.claim: Al-Suddī says God measured the fetus’s gestation as nine months or less or more and guided it to emerge once complete.
ALUSI:87:3/r8.anchor: وعن السدى قدر الولد في البطن تسعة أشهر أو أقل أو أكثر وهداه للخروج منه للتمام

ALUSI:87:3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:3/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:87:3/r9.claim: Another view says God measured benefits within things and guided humans to extract them.
ALUSI:87:3/r9.anchor: وقيل قدر المنافع في الأشياء وهدى الإنسان لاستخراجها

ALUSI:87:3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:3/r10.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers his initial general explanation and treats the other views as examples, not restrictions on the verse.
ALUSI:87:3/r10.anchor: والأولى ما ذكر أولاً ولعل ما في سائر الأقوال من باب التمثيل لا التخصيص

ALUSI:87:3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:3/r11.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI:87:3/r11.claim: Al-Farrāʾ claims the verse uses ellipsis, with “and misled” understood after “guided”; al-Ālūsī rejects this.
ALUSI:87:3/r11.anchor: وزعم الفراء أن في الآية اكتفاء والأصل فهدى وأضل وليس بشيء

ALUSI:87:3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:3/r12.speaker: الكسائي
ALUSI:87:3/r12.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads qaddara without doubling the dāl, deriving it from ability or estimation.
ALUSI:87:3/r12.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي قدر بالتخفيف من القدرة أو التقدير

BAGHAWI:87:3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:3/r1.speaker: الكسائي
BAGHAWI:87:3/r1.claim: Al-Kisa'i reads qadara with a light dāl; the other readers double it, and both forms have the same meaning.
BAGHAWI:87:3/r1.anchor: قرأ الكسائي : { قدر } بتخفيف الدال ، وشددها الآخرون ، وهما بمعنىً واحد .

BAGHAWI:87:3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI:87:3/r2.claim: Mujahid says God guided humans to good and evil, felicity and misery, and guided livestock to their grazing places.
BAGHAWI:87:3/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد : هدى الإنسان لسبيل الخير والشر ، والسعادة والشقاوة وهدى الأنعام لمراتعها .

BAGHAWI:87:3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:3/r3.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
BAGHAWI:87:3/r3.claim: Muqatil and al-Kalbi say God determined each thing's course and guided creatures to know how to mate as male and female.
BAGHAWI:87:3/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل والكلبي : قدر لكل شيء مسلكه ، { فهدى } : عرفها كيف يأتي الذكر والأنثى .

BAGHAWI:87:3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:3/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:87:3/r4.claim: Another view says God determined provisions and guided creatures to acquire their livelihood.
BAGHAWI:87:3/r4.anchor: وقيل : قدر الأرزاق وهدى لاكتساب الأرزاق والمعاش .

BAGHAWI:87:3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:3/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:87:3/r5.claim: Another view says God created benefits within things and guided people to extract them.
BAGHAWI:87:3/r5.anchor: وقيل : خلق المنافع في الأشياء ، وهدى الإنسان لوجه استخراجها منها .

BAGHAWI:87:3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:3/r6.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI:87:3/r6.claim: Al-Suddi says God determined the fetus's time in the womb and then guided it out of the womb.
BAGHAWI:87:3/r6.anchor: وقال السدي : قدر مدة الجنين في الرحم ثم هداه للخروج من الرحم .

BAGHAWI:87:3/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:3/r7.speaker: الواسطي
BAGHAWI:87:3/r7.claim: Al-Wasiti says God decreed people's felicity or misery and then enabled each group to follow the path decreed for it.
BAGHAWI:87:3/r7.anchor: قال الواسطي : قدر السعادة والشقاوة عليهم ، ثم يسر لكل واحد من الطائفتين سلوك سبيل ما قدر عليه .

BAYDAWI:87:3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:3/r1.claim: God determined the kinds, species, individuals, measures, qualities, acts, and lifespans of things.
BAYDAWI:87:3/r1.anchor: قدر أجناس الأشياء وأنواعها وأشخاصها ومقاديرها وصفاتها وأفعالها وآجالها

BAYDAWI:87:3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:3/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:3/r2.claim: He guides creatures to their acts by nature and choice, creating inclinations and inspirations, setting up signs, and sending verses.
BAYDAWI:87:3/r2.anchor: فوجهه إلى أفعاله طبعا واختيارا بخلق الميول والإلهامات ونصب الدلائل وانزال الآيات

BIQAI:87:2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:2/r4.speaker: الأستاذ أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:87:2/r4.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr connects the disbelievers' plot in al-Ṭāriq with the command to glorify God, then reads creation, proportion, ordainment, and guidance as evidence of divine power and wisdom against their slander.
BIQAI:87:2/r4.anchor: وقال الاستاذ أبو جعفر ابن الزبير

BIQAI:87:3/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:3/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:3/r1.claim: God assigns measures and conditions to kinds, species, individuals, amounts, qualities, acts, lifespans, and every other circumstance.
BIQAI:87:3/r1.anchor: أوقع تقديره في أجناس الأشياء وأنواعها

BIQAI:87:3/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:3/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:3/r2.claim: God fits faculties and forms to their purposes, creates natural or chosen inclinations and inspirations, and sets signs to avert harm and secure benefit.
BIQAI:87:3/r2.anchor: أوقع بسبب تقديره وعقبه الهداية لذلك الذي وقع التقدير من أجله من الشكل والجواهر والأعراض

BIQAI:87:3/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:3/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:3/r3.claim: A newborn instinctively opens its mouth to nurse, and other animals find what benefits them; creation needs proportion for balance, and ordainment needs guidance for perfection.
BIQAI:87:3/r3.anchor: فترى الطفل أول ما يقع من البطن يفتح فاه للرضاعة ، وغيره من سائر الحيوانات

BIQAI:87:3/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:3/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:3/r4.claim: The coordinating wāw links ordainment to proportion to signal that these attributes are firmly established together.
BIQAI:87:3/r4.anchor: أتبعه به بالواو دلالة على تمكن الأوصاف

DURR:87:3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:87:3/r1.claim: Mujāhid says God guided humans toward wretchedness or happiness and livestock to their grazing places.
DURR:87:3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : { والذي قدر فهدى } قال : هدى الإنسان للشقوة والسعادة ،   وهدى الأنعام لمراتعها .

IBNASHUR:87:2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:2/r9.claim: Determining means setting and producing a measure in things’ essences and powers; the doubled and undoubled forms of the verb have the same meaning.
IBNASHUR:87:2/r9.anchor: والتقديرُ : وضع المقدار وإيجاده في الأشياء في ذواتها وقواها ، يقال : قدّر بالتضعيف وقدَر بالتخفيف بمعنىً

IBNASHUR:87:2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:2/r10.speaker: الجمهور والكسائي
IBNASHUR:87:2/r10.claim: The majority read qaddara with a doubled d; al-Kisaʾi alone reads the lighter qad(a)ra form.
IBNASHUR:87:2/r10.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بالتشديد وقرأها الكسائي وحده بالتخفيف

IBNASHUR:87:2/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:2/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:2/r11.claim: Measure first means quantity fixed by length, volume, weight, or count; here it means creatures’ orderly, consistent structures and powers, including bodily parts, senses, and capacities for craft.
IBNASHUR:87:2/r11.anchor: والمقدار : أصله كمية الشيء التي تضبط بالذرع أو الكيل أو الوزن أو العدّ ، وأطلق هنا على تكوين المخلوقات

IBNASHUR:87:3/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:3/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:3/r1.claim: Repeating the relative pronoun before determined and brought forth the pasture emphasizes each predicate, an instance of amplification.
IBNASHUR:87:3/r1.anchor: وإعادة اسم الموصول في قوله : { والذي قدر } وقوله : { والذي أخرج المرعى } مع إغناء حرف العطف عن تكريره

IBNASHUR:87:3/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:3/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:3/r2.claim: The fa before guided works like the fa before shaped, marking the relation between the two clauses.
IBNASHUR:87:3/r2.anchor: وعطف قوله : { فهدى } بالفاء مثل عطف { فسوى }

IBNASHUR:87:3/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:3/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:3/r3.claim: Guidance is the result of determination: each determined creature is directed toward its allotted function, and fulfilling each aspect of its design entails guidance toward its use.
IBNASHUR:87:3/r3.anchor: وعطف { فهدى } على { قدر } عطف المسبب على السبب أي فهدى كل مقدر إلى ما قدر له

IBNASHUR:87:3/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:3/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:3/r4.claim: For humans and animals with perception and will, divine guidance inspires them to use their endowed powers appropriately.
IBNASHUR:87:3/r4.anchor: فهداية الإنسان وأنواع جنسه من الحيوان الذي له الإدراك والإرادة هي هداية الإلهام

IBNASHUR:87:3/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:3/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:3/r5.claim: Examples include human capacities for speech, knowledge, and craft; a cow’s grazing and nursing; and bees’ gathering nectar and building honeycomb cells.
IBNASHUR:87:3/r5.anchor: فالله لما قدر للإنسان أن يكون قابلا للنطق والعلم والصناعة بما وهبه من العقل وآلات الجسد

IBNASHUR:87:3/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:3/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:3/r6.claim: The reproductive powers given to animals are among the clearest signs of determination and guidance because they preserve the species.
IBNASHUR:87:3/r6.anchor: ومن أجل مظاهر التقدير والهداية تقدير قوى التناسل للحيوان لبقاء النوع

IBNASHUR:87:3/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:3/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:3/r7.claim: The object of guided is general in wording but limited to beings capable of guidance; fruiting trees and seed production are determined, not guided, because they cannot apprehend a direction.
IBNASHUR:87:3/r7.anchor: فمفعول « هدى » محذوف لإفادة العموم وهو عام مخصوص بما فيه قابلية الهدي

IBNASHUR:87:3/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:3/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:3/r8.claim: If created refers specifically to the human being, then determined means completing human faculties and guided means the direction supplied by perception and reason.
IBNASHUR:87:3/r8.anchor: وإن جعل مفعول { خلق } خاصاً ، وهو الإنسان كان مفعول { قدر } على وزانه ، أي تقدير كمال قوى الإنسان

IBNASHUR:87:3/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:3/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:3/r9.claim: Shaping and guidance suit the sura’s subject: the One who fitted the Prophet for his mission will prepare him to retain revelation and ease his task and law.
IBNASHUR:87:3/r9.anchor: فإن الذي يسوي خلق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تسوية تلائم ما خلقه لأجله من تحمل أعباء الرسالة

IBNATIYYA:87:3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:3/r1.speaker: جمهور القراء
IBNATIYYA:87:3/r1.claim: Most readers pronounce qaddara with a doubled dāl; Ibn Atiyya allows it to derive either from decree or from measuring and proportioning.
IBNATIYYA:87:3/r1.anchor: وقرأ جمهور القراء «قدّر » بشد الدال فيحتمل أن يكون من القدر والقضاء ،

IBNATIYYA:87:3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:3/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNATIYYA:87:3/r2.claim: Al-Farra says “He guided” implies both guidance and misguidance, mentioning one because it indicates the other.
