IBNATIYYA:87:3/r2.anchor: فقال الفراء : معناه هدى وأضل ، واكتفى بالواحدة لدلالتها على الأخرى

IBNATIYYA:87:3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:3/r3.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
IBNATIYYA:87:3/r3.claim: Muqatil and al-Kalbi say God guided animals to mating, directing males to females.
IBNATIYYA:87:3/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل والكلبي : هدى الحيوان إلى وطء الذكور الإناث

IBNATIYYA:87:3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:3/r4.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA:87:3/r4.claim: One reported example is that God guides a newborn, upon birth, to suckle at the breast.
IBNATIYYA:87:3/r4.anchor: هدى المولود عند وضعه إلى مص الثدي

IBNATIYYA:87:3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:3/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA:87:3/r5.claim: Mujahid says God guides people to good and evil, and animals to their pastures.
IBNATIYYA:87:3/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد : هدى الناس للخير والشر ،

IBNATIYYA:87:3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:87:3/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya treats these as examples and prefers the verse's general scope: God determines every matter and grants every kind of guidance.
IBNATIYYA:87:3/r6.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد : وهذه الأقوال مثالات ، والعموم في الآية أصوب في كل تقدير وفي كل هداية

IBNKATHIR:87:3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR:87:3/r1.claim: Mujāhid says God guided humans to misery or happiness and livestock to their grazing places.
IBNKATHIR:87:3/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد : هدى الإنسان للشقاوة والسعادة ، وهدى الأنعام لمراتعها

IBNKATHIR:87:3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:87:3/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir explains that God determined a measure and guided creatures toward it, paralleling Moses’s statement to Pharaoh.
IBNKATHIR:87:3/r2.anchor: أي : قدر قدرا ، وهدى الخلائق إليه

IBNKATHIR:87:3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:3/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR:87:3/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAmr reports the Prophet’s statement that God decreed all creatures’ measures fifty thousand years before creating the heavens and earth; the report adds that His Throne was on water.
IBNKATHIR:87:3/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله ابن عمرو : أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : " إن الله قَدَّر مقادير الخلائق

MAWARDI:87:3/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI:87:3/r1.claim: Mujahid says God decreed misery and happiness, and guided toward right conduct and misguidance.
MAWARDI:87:3/r1.anchor: قدّر الشقاوة والسعادة ،   وهداه للرشد والضلالة ،   قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI:87:3/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:3/r2.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:87:3/r2.claim: Another view says God apportioned provisions and food, and guided humans to their livelihood and wild animals to their pastures.
MAWARDI:87:3/r2.anchor: قدر أرزاقهم وأقواتهم ،   وهداهم لمعاشهم إن كانوا إنساً ،   ولمراعيهم إن كانوا وحشاً

MAWARDI:87:3/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:3/r3.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI:87:3/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says God made them male and female and guided the male in approaching the female.
MAWARDI:87:3/r3.anchor: قدرهم ذكوراً وإناثاً ،   وهدى الذكر كيف يأتي الأنثى ،   قاله السدي

MAWARDI:87:3/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:3/r4.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:87:3/r4.claim: A fourth possibility is that God determined their formation in the womb and guided them to emerge fully formed.
MAWARDI:87:3/r4.anchor: قدر خلقهم في الأرحام ،   وهداهم الخروج للتمام

MAWARDI:87:3/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:3/r5.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:87:3/r5.claim: A fifth possibility is that God created them for recompense and guided them to action.

NASAFI:87:3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:3/r1.claim: God apportioned to every animal what sustains it, then guided it to that provision and taught it how to benefit from it.
NASAFI:87:3/r1.anchor: قدر لكل حيوان ما يصلحه فهداه إليه وعرفه وجه الانتفاع به

NASAFI:87:3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:3/r2.claim: Alternatively, ‘guided’ implies that God also misguides, with ‘and misguides’ omitted because it is understood from parallels.
NASAFI:87:3/r2.anchor: أو فهدى وأضل ولكن حذف وأضل اكتفاء كقوله

QURTUBI:87:3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:3/r1.speaker: علي والسلمي والكسائي
QURTUBI:87:3/r1.claim: Ali, al-Sulami, and al-Kisa'i read qadara with light d; others double it. Al-Qurtubi says the readings mean the same.
QURTUBI:87:3/r1.anchor: قرأ علي رضي الله عنه والسلمي والكسائي  " قدر " مخففة الدال ، وشدد الباقون . وهما بمعنى واحد

QURTUBI:87:3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:3/r2.claim: God apportioned and fitted each kind to its form, then guided it by showing the way.
QURTUBI:87:3/r2.anchor: أي قدر ووفق لكل شكل شكل . " فهدى " أي أرشد

QURTUBI:87:3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:3/r3.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI:87:3/r3.claim: Mujahid says God decreed misery and happiness and guided toward right and error.
QURTUBI:87:3/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد : قدر الشقاوة والسعادة ، وهدى للرشد والضلالة

QURTUBI:87:3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:3/r4.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI:87:3/r4.claim: Mujahid also says God guides people to happiness and misery, and livestock to their pastures.
QURTUBI:87:3/r4.anchor: وعنه قال : هدى الإنسان للسعادة والشقاوة ، وهدى الأنعام لمراعيها

QURTUBI:87:3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:3/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:3/r5.claim: Another gloss says God apportioned provisions and livelihoods, guiding humans to their means of life and animals to grazing.

QURTUBI:87:3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي ومقاتل والكلبي
QURTUBI:87:3/r6.claim: These authorities say God taught creatures how the male approaches the female, as in 20:50.
QURTUBI:87:3/r6.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس والسدي ومقاتل والكلبي في قوله  " فهدى " قالوا : عرف خلقه كيف يأتي الذكر الأنثى

QURTUBI:87:3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:3/r7.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI:87:3/r7.claim: Ata says God gave each animal what benefits it and guided it to that.
QURTUBI:87:3/r7.anchor: وقال عطاء : جعل لكل دابة ما يصلحها ، وهداها له

QURTUBI:87:3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:3/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:3/r8.claim: One view says God created useful properties in things and guided people to extract and use them.
QURTUBI:87:3/r8.anchor: وقيل : خلق المنافع في الأشياء ، وهدى الإنسان

QURTUBI:87:3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:3/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:3/r9.claim: Another view says God determined what each animal needs, guided it, and showed how to benefit from it.

QURTUBI:87:3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:3/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:3/r10.claim: An illustrative account says a thousand-year-old blind snake is inspired to travel to fennel, rub its eyes on fresh leaves, and regain sight by God's permission.
QURTUBI:87:3/r10.anchor: يحكى أن الأفعى إذا أتت عليها ألف سنة عميت

QURTUBI:87:3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:3/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:3/r11.claim: Human needs in food, medicine, worldly and religious life, and the inspirations of animals, birds, and earth's creatures are too vast to describe or exhaust.
QURTUBI:87:3/r11.anchor: وهدايات الإنسان إلى ما لا يحد من مصالحه

QURTUBI:87:3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:3/r12.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI:87:3/r12.claim: Al-Suddi says God determined the embryo's period in the womb (nine months, sometimes less or more), then guided it out.
QURTUBI:87:3/r12.anchor: وقال السدي : قدر مدة الجنين في الرحم تسعة أشهر

QURTUBI:87:3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:3/r13.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI:87:3/r13.claim: Al-Farra says the phrase includes predestination, guidance, and misguidance, with one opposite implicit, as in 16:81, which mentions protection from heat alone.
QURTUBI:87:3/r13.anchor: وقال الفراء : أي قدر ، فهدى وأضل ، فاكتفى بذكر أحدهما

QURTUBI:87:3/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:3/r14.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:3/r14.claim: The verb may mean inviting people to faith, as in 42:52; God invited everyone to faith.
QURTUBI:87:3/r14.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون بمعنى دعا إلى الإيمان

QURTUBI:87:3/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:3/r15.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:87:3/r15.claim: Another view says God showed people through His acts that He is one, knowing, and powerful.

QURTUBI:87:3/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:3/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:3/r16.claim: All agree doubled d derives from estimation, as in 25:2; light d may mean the same or derive from qadr as possession: God owns things and guides whom He wills.
QURTUBI:87:3/r16.anchor: ولا خلاف أن من شدد الدال من " قدر " أنه من التقدير

QURTUBI:87:3/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:3/r17.speaker: بعض أشياخي
QURTUBI:87:3/r17.claim: A teacher of al-Qurtubi's said these clauses explain God's exaltedness over all creatures in a way befitting His majesty.
QURTUBI:87:3/r17.anchor: سمعت بعض أشياخي يقول : الذي خلق فسوى وقدر فهدى

RAZI:87:2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:87:2/r1.claim: After commanding glorification, God answers the implicit question of how the Lord is known by pointing to His creation and guidance.
RAZI:87:2/r1.anchor: لما أمر بالتسبيح ، فكأن سائلا قال :

RAZI:87:2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:87:2/r2.claim: Rāzī calls creation and guidance a major prophetic proof, citing Abraham’s statement that his Creator guides him.
RAZI:87:2/r2.anchor: عن إبراهيم عليه السلام ، أنه قال : { الذي خلقني

RAZI:87:2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:87:2/r3.claim: Moses answered Pharaoh’s question about the Lord by describing Him as the giver of each thing’s form and its guide.
RAZI:87:2/r3.anchor: قال موسى عليه السلام : { ربنا الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى

RAZI:87:2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:87:2/r4.claim: The opening revelation first points to creation and then to teaching, showing the same proof through creation and guidance.
RAZI:87:2/r4.anchor: ثم قال : { اقرأ وربك الأكرم الذي علم بالقلم } وهذا إشارة إلى الهداية

RAZI:87:2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:87:2/r5.claim: Creation and guidance are especially forceful evidence because their marvels are abundant and humans can observe them closely.
RAZI:87:2/r5.anchor: العجائب والغرائب في هذه الطريقة أكثر

RAZI:87:3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:3/r1.speaker: الجمهور
RAZI:87:3/r1.claim: The majority read qaddara with a doubled dāl: God assigned every thing a known measure.
RAZI:87:3/r1.anchor: قرأ الجمهور : { قدر } مشددة وقرأ الكسائي

RAZI:87:3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:3/r2.speaker: الكسائي
RAZI:87:3/r2.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads the verb with a light dāl; al-Qaffāl explains it as “owned,” meaning God owns what He created and directs it to its interests.
RAZI:87:3/r2.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي على التخفيف ، أما قراءة

RAZI:87:3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:87:3/r3.claim: Some grammarians treat the doubled and undoubled forms as two dialects with the same meaning, citing the variant forms in 77:23.
RAZI:87:3/r3.anchor: ومنهم من قال : هما لغتان بمعنى واحد

RAZI:87:3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:87:3/r4.claim: God apportioned created things in their essences and attributes: their sizes, durations, qualities, positions, beauty, misery, guidance, and misguidance.
RAZI:87:3/r4.anchor: قوله : { قدر } يتناول المخلوقات في ذواتها

RAZI:87:3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:87:3/r5.claim: In the bodily order, proportioning arranges components to receive particular faculties; guidance creates those faculties in organs so their acts produce complete benefit.
RAZI:87:3/r5.anchor: فالتسوية والتقدير عبارة عن التصرف في الأجزاء الجسمانية وتركيبها على وجه خاص

RAZI:87:3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:3/r6.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI:87:3/r6.claim: Mujāhid’s reported explanation from Muqātil is that God guided the male to the female and showed him how to approach her.
RAZI:87:3/r6.anchor: قال مقاتل : هدى الذكر للأنثى كيف يأتيها

RAZI:87:3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:87:3/r7.claim: Other commentators understand guidance as showing each creature how to obtain its livelihood and caring for it.

RAZI:87:3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:87:3/r8.claim: Another view is that God guides people to good and evil, happiness and misery, by giving them perception and the ability to pursue benefit and avoid harm.
RAZI:87:3/r8.anchor: هدى الإنسان لسبل الخير والشر والسعادة والشقاوة

RAZI:87:3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:3/r9.speaker: السدي
RAZI:87:3/r9.claim: Al-Suddī says God determined the fetus’s time in the womb and guided it to emerge.
RAZI:87:3/r9.anchor: قال السدي : قدر مدة الجنين في الرحم

RAZI:87:3/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:3/r10.speaker: الفراء
RAZI:87:3/r10.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says “guided” implies both guidance and misguidance, with one side omitted, as in the verse mentioning garments that protect from heat.

RAZI:87:3/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:3/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:87:3/r11.claim: Some take guidance to mean calling people to faith, as in the statement that the Prophet guides, meaning invites; all people were invited.

RAZI:87:3/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:3/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:87:3/r12.claim: Others understand guidance as God’s acts serving as signs of His oneness, majesty, self-sufficiency, and uniqueness to rational observers.
RAZI:87:3/r12.anchor: وقال آخرون : هدى أي دلهم بأفعاله

RAZI:87:3/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:3/r13.speaker: قتادة
RAZI:87:3/r13.claim: Qatāda says God does not compel or command anyone to sin or misguidance, but approves obedience, commands it, and forbids sin.
RAZI:87:3/r13.anchor: وقال قتادة في قوله : { فهدى } إن الله تعالى

RAZI:87:3/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:3/r14.speaker: author
RAZI:87:3/r14.claim: Rāzī groups the explanations into worldly guidance and religious guidance, preferring the latter: after creation, proportioning, and human faculties, “guided” means made responsible and directed to religion.
RAZI:87:3/r14.anchor: والأول أقوى ، لأن قوله : { خلق فسوى والذي قدر }

QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r5.claim: God measures each created thing to His intention and guides animals through inspiration to take what benefits them and avoid harm.
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r5.anchor: قدر ما خلقه ، فجعله على مقدار ما أراده

QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r6.claim: God guides heedless hearts to build the world, while worshippers seek and prefer the afterlife.
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r6.anchor: هدى قلوب الغافلين إلى طلب الدنيا فعمروها

QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r7.claim: God guides ascetics to recognize the world's passing nature and reject it.
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r7.anchor: هدى قلوب الزاهدين إلى فناء الدنيا فرفضوها

QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r8.claim: God guides scholars to examine His signs and infer from His creations, so they recognize and remain with those signs.
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r8.anchor: هدى قلوب العلماء إلى النظر في آياته والاستدلال بمصنوعاته

QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r9.claim: God guides seekers to the glory of His attribute; they prefer Him, devote their effort, and seek Him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r9.anchor: هدى قلوب المريدين إلى عز وصفه فآثروه

QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r10.claim: God guides the gnostics to the sanctity of His description, where they watch and then witness Him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r10.anchor: هدى العارفين إلى قدس نعته فراقبوه ثم شاهدوه

QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r11.claim: God guides monotheists to His sovereign sublimity; they abandon familiar things and seek Him alone.
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r11.anchor: هدى الموحدين إلى علاء سلطانه في تحد كبريائه

QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r12.claim: Beyond proof, explanation, and near-vision, the knowers find God inaccessible beyond separation and union, and make incapacity their resting place.
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r12.anchor: علموا أنه عزيز ، وأنه وراء كل فصل ووصل

FARRA:v3p256/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p256/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p256/r2.claim: 'Measured and guided' can mean God measured creation and guided male animals to the mating place of females.
FARRA:v3p256/r2.anchor: قدر خلقه فهدى الذكر لمأتى الأنثى من البهائم

FARRA:v3p256/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p256/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p256/r3.claim: Alternatively, 'measured, guided, and led astray' omits mention of misguidance because it is often paired with guidance.
FARRA:v3p256/r3.anchor: فاكتفى من ذكر الضلال بذكر الهدى لكثرة ما يكون معه

FARRA:v3p256/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p256/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p256/r4.claim: Reciters agree on doubled qaddara; al-Sulami's lighter reading is attributed to Ali.
FARRA:v3p256/r4.anchor: وكان أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي يقرأ: قدر مخففة

FARRA:v3p256/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p256/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p256/r5.claim: Al-Farra prefers the doubled reading because the reciters agree on it.
FARRA:v3p256/r5.anchor: والتشديد أحب إلي لاجتماع القراء عليه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.claim: The preceding sūrah urges the Prophet to wait: persistent deniers receive only temporary respite under God's practice, and cannot escape His grasp.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.anchor: Sūrah al-Ṭāriq, the previous sūrah ended on urging the Prophet (sws) to show patience and to wait for the decision of God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.claim: This sūrah shifts its primary address from stubborn Quraysh to the Prophet and, over at least ten following sūrahs, dispels his preaching fears in varied ways.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.anchor: while ignoring these stubborn elements from among the Quraysh, the Prophet (sws) is addressed directly and given glad tidings

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r3.claim: Verses 1–5 direct the Prophet to glorify God, whose attributes show that creation and human physical and intellectual capacities mature gradually.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p274/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p274/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p274/r2.claim: God develops material and spiritual abilities, implants needs, and supplies the means and capacity to meet them, as in an infant guided to its mother's milk.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p274/r2.anchor: if a child needs milk, then he has been provided with it through the bosoms of his mother

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p274/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p274/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p274/r3.claim: The verse comprehensively covers moral awareness, prophetic guidance, and life's appointed trials: God's way leads to salvation, while deviation and whims lead to ruin.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p274/r3.anchor: the Almighty has ingrained in him the awareness of good and evil and sent prophets and messengers to him for his guidance

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r8.claim: The majority read qaddara with doubled dāl, allowing meanings of decree or measured proportion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: قدر بشد الدال، فاحتمل أن يكون من القدر والقضاء،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says God assigned each animal what suits it, guided it to that provision, and taught it how to benefit from it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r9.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: قدر لكل حيوان ما يصلحه، فهداه إليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r10.speaker: الكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r10.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads qaddara with a light dāl, deriving it from power or measurement and proportion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r10.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي: قدر مخفف الدال من القدرة أو من التقدير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r11.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r11.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the mention of guidance suffices while its opposite, leading astray, is left implicit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r11.anchor: وقال الفراء: فهدى وأضل، اكتفى بالواحدة عن الأخرى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r12.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r12.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil say God guided animals to mate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r12.anchor: وقال الكلبي ومقاتل: هدى الحيوان إلى وطء الذكور للإناث.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r13.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r13.claim: Mujāhid says humans are guided to good and evil, while livestock are guided to grazing grounds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r13.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هدى الإنسان للخير والشر، والبهائم للمراتع.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r14.claim: Another view is that a newborn is guided to suckle; the cited accounts are examples, not exclusive interpretations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r14.anchor: وقيل: هدى المولود عند وضعه إلى مص الثدي، وهذه الأقوال محمولة

DURR-FULL:v8p482/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r6.claim: God guides humans toward happiness or misery and guides livestock to their grazing places.
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {والذي قدر فهدى}

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r2.claim: Its purposes include glorifying God and indicating His oneness through His unique creation of humans and earthly sustenance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p272/r2.anchor: تنزيه الله تعالى والإشارة إلى وحدانيته لانفراده بخلق الإنسان وخلق ما في الأرض مما فيه بقاؤه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p277/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p277/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p277/r1.claim: Reproductive powers suited to animal life and preservation of species are among the clearest instances of divine ordaining and guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p277/r1.anchor: ومن أجل مظاهر التقدير والهداية تقدير قوى التناسل للحيوان لبقاء النوع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p277/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p277/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p277/r2.claim: The object of guided is omitted for generality, then restricted to beings capable of guidance: animals with perception and will, not fruiting or seed-producing plants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p277/r2.anchor: محذوف لإفادة العموم وهو عام مخصوص بما فيه قابلية الهدي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p277/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p277/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p277/r3.claim: Proportioning and guidance suit the surah because God who fashioned the Prophet for the burdens of mission also equips him to retain revelation and grants him an easy law.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p277/r3.anchor: الذي يسوي خلق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تسوية تلائم ما خلقه لأجله من تحمل أعباء الرسالة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r4.claim: The majority read qaddara with a doubled d; it can mean decree or determine by measure.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r4.anchor: وقرأ جمهور القراء «قدر» بشد الدال فيحتمل أن يكون من القدر والقضاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r5.speaker: الفراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r5.claim: Al-Farra glosses guidance as both guiding and leading astray, with the stated half implying its counterpart.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r5.anchor: فقال الفراء: معناه هدى وأضل، واكتفى بالواحدة لدلالتها على الأخرى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r6.speaker: مقاتل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r6.claim: Muqatil and al-Kalbi say God guides animals to mating.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل والكلبي: هدى الحيوان إلى وطء الذكور الإناث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r7.claim: Another view says God guides a newborn, upon delivery, to suckle at the breast.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r7.anchor: وقيل هدى المولود عند وضعه إلى مص الثدي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r8.claim: Mujahid says people are guided to good or evil and livestock to their grazing places.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r8.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هدى الناس للخير والشر، والبهائم للمراتع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r9.claim: These interpretations are examples; the soundest reading keeps the verse general across kinds of ordaining and guidance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r9.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذه الأقوال مثالات، والعموم في الآية أصوب في كل تقدير

JISHUMI:v10p7372/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r1.claim: The surah follows the preceding warning of unbelievers with God’s attributes and power to do whatever He wills.
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r1.anchor:
ما يشاء.
(بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم)
قوله تعالى:

JISHUMI:v10p7372/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r2.speaker: الكسائي وعلي بن أبي طالب وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r2.claim: They read qaddara with a light dāl; the other readers use the doubled form, which may mean the same or distinguish power from apportionment.
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r2.anchor: قرأ الكسائي: قدر خفيفة، وهي قراءة علي بن أبي طالب وأبي عبد الرحمن السلمي، وقرأ الآخرون بالتشديد

JISHUMI:v10p7372/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r7.claim: Taqdīr is managing something according to a measured amount; hidāyah is guidance to right conduct.
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r7.anchor: التقدير: تدبير الشيء على مقدار، قدره تقديرا. والهداية: الدلالة على الرشد.

JISHUMI:v10p7373/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r18.claim: One view says God apportioned sustenance and guided creatures to seek it; Abu Ali says He apportioned forms and livelihoods and thereby guided them to know His oneness.
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r18.anchor: قيل: قدر القوت، وهدى لطلبه، وقيل: قدر الخلق على ما خلقهم من الصور والهيئات

JISHUMI:v10p7373/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r19.claim: Other views say He set lifespans and provisions, guided to monotheism through signs, or measured creation and completed reason to guide people to religion.
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r19.anchor: وقيل: قدر الآجال والأرزاق، وهدى إلى التوحيد بإظهار الآيات، وقيل: خلق على مقدار معلوم

JISHUMI:v10p7373/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r20.speaker: عطاء وأبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r20.claim: They say God allotted each animal what suits it and guided it to that provision.
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r20.anchor: وقيل: قدر لكل دابة ما يصلحها، وهداها إليها، عن عطاء، وأبي مسلم.

JISHUMI:v10p7373/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r21.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r21.claim: A universal reading says God measured and guided everything: infants find the breast, young birds find their mothers, and creatures seek their appointed sustenance.
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r21.anchor: فهدى الطفل إلى ثدي أمه، والفرخ إلى أمه، والدواب والطيور، فكل أحد يفزع إلى أمه

JISHUMI:v10p7373/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r22.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r22.claim: Mujahid interprets the guidance as direction to both good and evil.
JISHUMI:v10p7373/r22.anchor: وقيل: هدى لسبيل الخير والشر، عن مجاهد.

MUQATIL:87:1-7/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r3.speaker: مقاتل
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r3.claim: One explanation is that God sets the pregnancy at nine months and guides the child to leave the womb when the term arrives.
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r3.anchor: يقول: الذي قدر الولد في بطن أمه تسعة أشهر، فلما بلغ الوقت هداه

MUQATIL:87:1-7/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r4.speaker: مقاتل
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r4.claim: Another explanation is that God determines male and female and teaches each how to approach the other.
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r4.anchor: قدر الذكر والأنثى فعلمه، كيف يأتيها؟ وكيف تأتيه؟

TABATABAI:87:1-19/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r11.claim: God measures creatures and guides them through providence toward their appointed course.
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r11.anchor: فكل يسلك نحو ما قدر له بهداية ربانية تكوينية

TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r1.claim: The citations speak of known measure, making a path easy, and each person's direction.
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r1.anchor: وإن من شيء إلا عندنا خزائنه وما ننزله إلا بقدر معلوم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:1-6/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:1-6/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:1-6/r3.claim: God apportioned provisions and guided people to seek them.

TABATABAI:6:122-127/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:122-127/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:122-127/r1.claim: Guidance is of two kinds: creational direction of each kind and individual toward its created perfection, acts, appointed course, and lifespan; the Qur'an describes God as giving each thing its form and then guiding it.
TABATABAI:6:122-127/r1.anchor: وهدايته تعالى نوعان أحدهما الهداية التكوينية وهي التي تتعلق بالأمور التكوينية
